sourceCopy.name: FIRE Calculator
sourceCopy.title: FIRE Calculator Free | UsefulVerse
sourceCopy.description: Estimate a financial independence target and timeline from spending, withdrawal rate, savings, returns, and inflation. Free and private.
sourceCopy.intro: Estimate the portfolio target implied by your annual spending and chosen withdrawal rate, then model how current savings and monthly contributions might approach it.
sourceCopy.howQuestion: How do you calculate a FIRE number?
sourceCopy.howAnswer: Divide annual spending by a withdrawal-rate fraction. For example, 40,000 divided by 4% gives a 1,000,000 target. The timeline then applies the entered nominal-return and inflation assumptions to the current portfolio and monthly contributions.
sourceCopy.privacyAnswer: No. The scenario is calculated in this browser tab and is not uploaded or automatically saved.

fields.currencyNote: Use the same currency for all money amounts. Enter assumptions as percentages; the projection converts the entered nominal return and inflation into a real growth rate.
fields.accuracyNote: Scenario math only. Returns, inflation, spending, taxes, fees, benefits, sequence risk, and future rules are uncertain or not modeled. This is not investment, tax, or retirement advice; it does not promise financial independence.
fields.privacyNote: Your entries stay in this browser tab. They are not uploaded or automatically saved.
fields.formulaNote: Target portfolio = annual spending ÷ (withdrawal rate ÷ 100). Timeline applies monthly real growth derived from your entered nominal return and inflation, then adds each monthly contribution at month-end.
fields.projectedBalance: Projected balance at target or 100-year limit
fields.unreachable: Target not reached within the 100-year projection

actions.privacyNote: Names and pairings stay on this device.

additionalFaqs.question: What is the FIRE target formula?
additionalFaqs.answer: This tool divides annual spending by the withdrawal-rate fraction you enter. At 40,000 annual spending and 4%, that arithmetic target is 1,000,000; it is not a guarantee that the amount will last.

additionalFaqs.question: Does the calculator guarantee a date for financial independence?
additionalFaqs.answer: No. It illustrates one deterministic scenario from your assumptions. Actual returns and inflation vary, while taxes, fees, changing spending, benefits, and sequence-of-returns risk can change outcomes.

additionalFaqs.question: Is a 4% withdrawal rate safe for everyone?
additionalFaqs.answer: This tool does not establish a safe rate. A rate’s suitability depends on horizon, portfolio, fees, taxes, inflation, market sequence, and individual circumstances. Consider qualified independent advice.
